What the fuck is up with Steven Universe?

It's a lot of things. It can be a comedy, or it could be an action show. It can flip between a gag and a dramatic scene just as easily. If you really want to boil it down, it's really just a family show and about a kid who's trying find his place in the world.

Steven is a one of a kind human/gem hybrid. Neither a full human nor a actual gem. He barely knows about his origins from both sides. He lives on the outskirts of town and the only education he received was from his father. He never attended school so he doesn't have many people his age to speak with. He gets barely anything from his gem caretakers who've rarely told them what they are or were. There's a lot of things Steven doesn't know about his gem abilities as well as the mother who gave birth to him. A lot of tough questions for a young child with people who are hesitant or just plain unable to answer. That's what makes it interesting. Those questions we want to see answer as much as Steven.

As for pandering to the progressives... yeah. Those elements are there, but they're not really the core of the show and it doesn't get in the way of telling the story. They don't try to make a big deal about there being lesbians or how the town is multicultural and diverse. I honestly don't even notice most of that, because I'm focused on the relationships between the characters. The only time you'll see it right in your face is with Garnet (the tall afro one) and though they try to hide it with "It's not about lesbians, it's about two different gems fusing", we know it's really a metaphor for same-sex couples.
